objectives.statement: Explain model binding as the ASP.NET Core process that obtains request data and populates action parameters or model properties.
Identify ModelState as the record of bound data and binding or validation errors, and ModelState.IsValid as the success check.
Distinguish the standard binding sources FromQuery, FromRoute, FromForm and FromBody by the part of the HTTP request from which each obtains values.
Explain that FromBody delegates request-body reading to an input formatter and should not be applied to more than one action parameter.
Explain how model binding searches for prefixed and unprefixed property names when binding a complex type.
Explain that model validation occurs after model binding and before a controller action or Razor Pages handler executes.
objectives.citation: Model validation in ASP.NET Core MVC and Razor Pages

objectives.statement: Distinguish model-binding conversion errors from model-validation errors caused by data that violates business rules.
objectives.citation: Model validation in ASP.NET Core MVC and Razor Pages

objectives.statement: Identify ModelState.IsValid as the check an MVC web application uses before proceeding with a valid model and saving changes.
objectives.citation: Model validation in ASP.NET Core MVC and Razor Pages

objectives.statement: Explain validation attributes as metadata that specify validation rules for model properties.

objectives.statement: Relate EF Core entity states Added, Modified and Deleted to the INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE commands produced by SaveChanges.
Explain that an entity passed to Add receives the Added state and is inserted when SaveChanges is called.
Explain the read-first edit pattern as retrieving an entity, allowing only selected properties to be updated, and then saving tracked changes.
objectives.citation: Use recommended HttpPost Edit code: Read and update

objectives.statement: Identify Bind or an input view model as a way to restrict fields accepted from user input and help prevent overposting.
Explain that EF Core's default SaveChanges transaction makes changes to multiple rows or tables succeed together or roll back together.
Explain that EF Core asynchronous query and save methods return tasks that must be awaited, and that parallel operations on one DbContext instance are not supported.
Identify asynchronous EF Core methods such as ToListAsync, FirstOrDefaultAsync and SaveChangesAsync as task-returning alternatives for database operations.
Relate an async MVC action to awaiting EF Core operations before returning an action result or continuing the unit of work.
Diagnose an invalid posted model as a case where the application should inspect ModelState and redisplay or return errors instead of saving the invalid data.
Apply the read-first and allowed-property approach to an edit request to preserve protected fields and avoid overposting while SaveChanges persists tracked modifications.
